issues.t: Head gasket failure and overheating (Northstar head bolts)
issues.sym: Coolant keeps disappearing, the engine overheats, white exhaust smoke, or exhaust bubbles in the coolant tank. Reports cluster around 70,000-140,000 miles.
issues.why: The Northstar V8's head bolts thread into the aluminum block, and the threads can pull out, especially after overheating. The head gasket then leaks combustion gas into the coolant.
issues.next: Stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs. A proper fix means installing threaded inserts in the block, which is a big job; get a quote from a shop experienced with Northstars before deciding.

issues.t: Engine burns oil
issues.sym: You have to add oil between changes, sometimes a quart every 1,000 miles or less, and may see blue smoke on start-up.
issues.why: GM issued several bulletins for higher-than-expected oil consumption and knocking on the Northstar, linked to piston ring deposits.
issues.next: Check the oil every fill-up. A dealer or shop can do a ring-cleaning procedure; if it is severe, engine work is needed.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the lower crankcase and oil pan
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, oil coating the bottom of the engine, or a burning smell from oil on the exhaust.
issues.why: The sealant between the Northstar's upper and lower crankcase halves and the oil pan breaks down. GM issued bulletins with improved sealing procedures.
issues.next: Watch your oil level. Small seeps can be lived with; a real leak needs the lower crankcase resealed, which is labor-heavy.

issues.t: Coolant leak from water pump cover or thermostat housing
issues.sym: Coolant smell, a low coolant warning, or drips near the front of the engine.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for coolant and oil leaks on the 4.6L, including a water pump cover leak and a loose thermostat.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and have the leak found quickly; running low on coolant risks the head gaskets.

issues.t: Engine stalls while driving or coming to a stop
issues.sym: The engine stumbles or dies when slowing down or stopping, or shuts off at highway speed and then restarts. Power steering and brake assist get heavy when it dies.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for stumbles and stalls when stopping. Owners also traced stalls to a failed camshaft or crankshaft sensor and a loose relay.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Shift to Neutral and restart if it happens. Have the codes read; sensors and software are common fixes.

issues.t: Check engine light with torque converter clutch slip
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0741 or P0742, a chuggle or surge at steady speed, firm shifts or shudder.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for the torque converter clutch slipping or sticking on the 4T80-E transmission.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked. Software, a solenoid or a torque converter may be needed.

issues.t: Transmission whine or no fourth gear
issues.sym: A whine at 20-50 mph under light throttle, fourth gear slipping, or no fourth gear at all.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for whine from worn sprocket thrust bearings and for fourth-gear slipping on the 4T80-E.
issues.next: Have the transmission inspected before it gets worse; internal repairs may avoid a full replacement.

issues.t: Power steering moan, leaks or loss of assist
issues.sym: A moan or squawk on low-speed turns, steering that feels heavy, or fluid leaks. Some owners reported the rack failing.
issues.why: GM issued many bulletins for power steering moan, and owners reported rack-and-pinion failures.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for leaks. A failing rack should be replaced before steering is lost.
issues.sevReason: Mostly moan/leak on a hydraulic system; gradual loss. First step covers sudden heaviness.

issues.t: Rust under the battery in the rear floor
issues.sym: Rust or holes in the floor under the rear seat battery area, sometimes a sulfur smell.
issues.why: The battery sits under the rear seat, and acid fumes or leaks corrode the floor. GM issued bulletins for this.
issues.next: Lift the rear seat and inspect the battery tray. Clean and treat rust early before it goes through the floor.

issues.t: Water inside headlights and taillights
issues.sym: Moisture or water in the lamps and bulbs that burn out often, especially after rain.
issues.why: Lamp seals let in water. GM issued guidance on lamp condensation, and owners reported it shorting bulbs.
issues.next: Have the lamp seals checked; a lamp that holds water usually needs replacing.

issues.t: Fuel rail and return line can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell under the hood. One owner reported an engine fire on start-up.
issues.why: GM recalled 1995-1997 models for leaking fuel rails and return lines.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, don't drive. Ask a dealer if the recall was done.

issues.t: Alternator can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before the problem; it can happen even when the car is off.
issues.why: An internal short in the alternator can overheat. GM replaced the generator under recall 99V070.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have a dealer confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Wipers stop on low speed (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop when switched from high to low.
issues.why: A fault in the wiper motor control. GM replaced the motor cover under recall 98V144.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Inner tie rod nuts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Loose or wandering steering; in the worst case the tie rod separates.
issues.why: Inner tie rod nuts can loosen. GM tightened them and set the alignment under recall 99V301.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: ABS unit can leak internally (recall)
issues.sym: ABS, traction or stability warnings; rear brake balance may be off.
issues.why: Internal leaks in the brake hydraulic unit can disable rear proportioning, ABS and stability control. GM inspected and replaced units under recall 00V114.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Steering gear bolt may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks or uneven steering response.
issues.why: Steering gear mounting bolts may be missing or loose, which could lead to a loss of steering control.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm recall 02V067 was done.

issues.t: Fuel tank pressure sensor can lead to fuel leaks (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or fuel leaking when you fill up.
issues.why: The fuel tank pressure sensor can fail and apply too much vacuum during self-tests, damaging fuel parts.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about recall 03V238; the sensor is replaced free.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch on the V6
issues.sym: Check engine light with cam/crank timing codes (P0008, P0009, P0016-P0019), rough running or rattling at start-up. Reports range from about 30,000 to 135,000 miles.
issues.why: The timing chains on GM's 3.6L V6 wear and stretch early, especially with long oil change intervals. GM issued a bulletin with timing chain kits and guides.
issues.next: Don't ignore these codes; a badly stretched chain can jump and bend valves. Change the oil on time and get a timing chain quote.

issues.t: Engine burns oil (V6)
issues.sym: Needing to add oil often, about a quart every 700 miles in one case. A low-oil warning may come on.
issues.why: Owners report piston ring problems causing oil consumption on the V6, and it is a top 2011 complaint.
issues.next: Check the oil level regularly; running low also speeds up timing chain wear. Have an oil consumption test done.

issues.t: Oil leak from Northstar V8 seals
issues.sym: Oil drips under the car and a burning smell.
issues.why: The Northstar V8 still uses sealed crankcase halves and seals that can leak. One owner reported a seal leak repair at about 70,000 miles.
issues.next: Watch the oil level and have the leak pinpointed.

issues.t: Transmission solenoid pack failure
issues.sym: Harsh or erratic shifts, slipping, or the transmission stuck in one gear with a warning light.
issues.why: The solenoid pack that controls shifts fails; CarComplaints owners report it at about 86,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read. Replacing the solenoid pack early can prevent damage to the rest of the transmission.

issues.t: A/C won't hold a charge (condenser leak)
issues.sym: A/C blows warm a short time after being recharged.
issues.why: The A/C condenser at the front of the car leaks refrigerant.
issues.next: Have a leak test done instead of just recharging. Replacing the condenser is the usual fix.

issues.t: Battery drains after the car is shut off
issues.sym: A dead battery after the car sits overnight or a few days.
issues.why: A module stays awake after shutdown and drains the battery; it is the most-reported 2006 STS complaint.
issues.next: Have a parasitic draw test done to find which circuit is draining it.

issues.t: Power steering fluid leaks
issues.sym: Power steering fluid on the ground, a whining pump, or heavy steering.
issues.why: Owners report leaking power steering lines, a corroded line bridge, and a leaking steering rack.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and have the leak found before the pump runs dry.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power steering ("Service Steering System")
issues.sym: Steering suddenly turns very stiff and a "Service Steering System" message appears. It may come back after the car cools down.
issues.why: Owners report the steering assist cutting out on the 2009 model, sometimes along with stability system faults.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Get it diagnosed before it happens at speed.

issues.t: Stability control fault and reduced engine power
issues.sym: A stability control warning followed by a reduced engine power message; the car slows to 10-15 mph.
issues.why: A fault in the stability system makes the car limit engine power.
issues.next: Get off the road safely, then have the codes read; wheel speed or steering sensors are common causes.

issues.t: Hard brake pedal from low brake assist
issues.sym: The brake pedal is very hard to push, especially at start-up, and stopping takes more effort.
issues.why: Owners report low brake booster assist, a blown vacuum assist fuse, and insufficient brake pressure at start-up. Brakes are the most-reported 2009 complaint.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Don't drive it if the pedal is hard; have the brake booster, vacuum pump and fuse checked.

issues.t: Moisture inside the headlights
issues.sym: Fog or water inside the headlights and bulbs that burn out or pop out.
issues.why: Headlight seals let moisture in. It is the top 2011 complaint.
issues.next: Have the headlight seals checked; a headlight that holds water often needs replacing.

issues.t: Dash lights, windows and sensors act up on their own
issues.sym: Instrument panel lights go out, the navigation quits, backup sensors chime for nothing, or windows move on their own. Some cars stalled.
issues.why: Owners report several electronic faults at once, which point to a module or wiring fault. GM issued a bulletin about powertrain and electronic control issues on the 2011 STS.
issues.next: Note when it happens and have the dealer check for module codes and bulletins.

issues.t: Rear axle pinion seal can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Fluid leaking near the rear differential. In one report, the differential failed with a bang and smoke.
issues.why: The pinion seal may not meet specification and can leak, which can cause the differential to fail. GM replaced the seal under recall.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Engine can stall when fuel is low (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stops below about a quarter tank, without the low fuel light or chime, and won't restart.
issues.why: Fuel can stop reaching the engine. GM reprogrammed the engine computer under recall.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Keep the tank above a quarter full and confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Throttle safety check not enabled on AWD V6 (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms before a failure; a computer fault could open the throttle more than you asked for.
issues.why: The electronic throttle's torque monitoring was not turned on. GM reprogrammed the engine computer under recall.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Rear toe link can separate (recall)
issues.sym: The car may wander or pull suddenly.
issues.why: A bad weld can let a rear toe link come apart. GM inspected and replaced links under recall.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning may not work (recall)
issues.sym: The low tire pressure warning doesn't come on when it should.
issues.why: The tire pressure system didn't meet the federal standard. GM reprogrammed the receiver module under recall.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall was done, and check tire pressures monthly.

issues.t: STS-V fuel pump module can melt and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell, or the engine stalls.
issues.why: Electrical terminals on the fuel pump module can overheat and melt the flange, leaking fuel. GM replaced the module and harness under recall.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. If you smell fuel, don't drive. Have a dealer confirm the recall was done.
